mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-2% mean) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-2% mean) when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 8% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 8% in one month compared to previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-2% mean) when UNRATE exceeds 8% in a single month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and reduces profit growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-2% mean) when INDPRO is below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous and persistent rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and accelerating inflation, which erodes real purchasing power and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month averages for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-2% mean) when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A strong and sustained increase in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals improved consumer purchasing power, which boosts demand and supports higher corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +2% mean) when PAYEMS exceeds its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated fall in both UNRATE and PAYEMS below their 12-month averages in the same month indicates a broad-based labor market weakening, which reduces aggregate demand and profit expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE and PAYEMS both fall below 12-month averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-2% mean) when both UNRATE and PAYEMS fall below their 12-month averages in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related economic activity and supports broader consumer confidence, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +2% mean) when HOUST is above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months.
